title: Instant Oatmeal, Plain, Made with Water, Fat Added

content.title: About
content.content: Instant oatmeal is made from whole or rolled oat grains that are steamed and dried, allowing preparation in 1–2 minutes by adding hot water. The “plain, made with water, fat added” version has a neutral flavor, is prepared with water, and includes a small amount of added fat (usually vegetable oil) to improve texture and increase energy density.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Oats are one of the oldest cultivated grains, grown for over 5,000 years.
Instant oatmeal retains most of the fiber and beta‑glucans that are beneficial for heart health.
Adding fat (typically vegetable oil) enhances the absorption of fat‑soluble vitamins and makes the meal more satiating.
Oat flakes can be used in baking, as a thickener for soups and sauces, and in homemade granola.
Oats are often called the “golden grain” because of their yellowish hue after processing.

items.title: Rich in beta‑glucans
items.content: Beta‑glucans help lower cholesterol and support immune function.

items.title: Source of complex carbohydrates
items.content: Provides slow‑release energy, helping maintain stable blood sugar levels.

items.title: Contains vitamin B1 and magnesium
items.content: Vitamin B1 aids carbohydrate metabolism, while magnesium supports muscle and nerve function.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: Fiber promotes regular bowel movements and a healthy gut microbiome.

items.title: Increases satiety
items.content: The added fat slows gastric emptying, prolonging the feeling of fullness.

items.title: Oat allergy
items.content: A small number of people may experience allergic reactions to oats or oat components.

items.title: Gluten cross‑contamination
items.content: Oats are often processed on the same equipment as wheat, so gluten contamination is possible.

items.title: Higher calorie content with added fat
items.content: The added fat increases the caloric density, so portion control is advisable.

items.title: Phytic acid content
items.content: Phytic acid can reduce mineral absorption; soaking or fermentation can lower its level.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Pour 200 ml of boiling water over the oatmeal, stir, and let it sit for 1–2 minutes. Optionally add fruit, nuts, honey, or spices. The added fat makes the porridge creamier and richer.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in a cool, dry place in a tightly sealed package. After opening, use within 1–2 weeks to maintain texture and prevent moisture absorption.
